title: How fast the in-game market ticks, and how big each step is
headline_insight: In-game MLB total-market quotes on Kalshi update at a median of 35.0 seconds between ticks, and each move is small -- a median 0.02 change in market probability.
what_it_means: This is the plumbing of a live prediction market: prices refresh on the order of tens of seconds and step in roughly two-cent increments, not big jumps. On the WNBA board the market's built-in spread (overround) sits near a penny at the median (0.01), which is how thin the quoted vig is.
how_to_read: inter_tick_seconds is the gap between consecutive quotes on the same market line; price_move_size is the absolute change in market probability between those ticks; overround is 1/home_decimal + 1/away_decimal - 1 per snapshot.
why_it_matters: Cadence and step size set the resolution of any live comparison -- you cannot react faster than the market prints, and small steps mean the tape moves in a steady drift rather than lurches.
caveat: Labelled a market-microstructure MEASUREMENT (latency/cadence), NOT a trading signal; sample is small (21 MLB quote tracks over 5 files; 2 WNBA files). The model-vs-market divergence figure in this artifact is a calibration-gap measurement, not an edge.
